rating_scale.0: Unusable: absent, materially wrong, unsupported, or misleading.
rating_scale.1: Major edit: the right subject is visible but a substantial rewrite or evidence repair is needed.
rating_scale.2: Minor edit: accurate and useful, with a limited clarity, focus, or completeness edit needed.
rating_scale.3: Ready: accurate, focused, complete for the evidence, and publishable as written.

dimensions.useful_detail: Names the concrete capability, limit, availability, or result a reader can act on.

dimensions.honest_uncertainty: Names material unknowns and does not convert marketing or silence into fact.
dimensions.readable_public_copy: Uses concise, specific language whose importance is clear on one read.

article.text: Atlas 2.0 became generally available on October 8, 2026, with signed Linux packages and an offline migration command. The release notes describe the migration command as a local conversion step for existing project files. They list packages for x86-64 and arm64 Linux systems and include checksums beside every download. The maintainers say macOS and Windows packages are still being tested, without promising a date. The document does not compare performance with other tools and gives no adoption figures. Operators can keep Atlas 1.x installed while validating a converted copy.

article.text: Northstar introduced a preview of its cache controls on October 8, 2026, and published configuration examples for opt-in testing. The controls let testers set a per-project retention window and clear individual cache namespaces. Northstar says its preview is twice as fast as every competing cache, but the post provides no benchmark data or comparison method. The preview is disabled by default and the company asks users to report eviction bugs. General availability, pricing, and compatibility outside the listed Linux test image remain unannounced. The configuration examples use only synthetic projects.

article.text: River's Windows client became generally available on October 8, 2026, after the Linux client shipped on October 1. The Windows build supports the same encrypted workspace format and can open workspaces created by the Linux release. The vendor documents Windows 11 as the supported operating system and provides signed installer checksums. Windows 10 is not listed. The announcement makes no claim about mobile support or market adoption. Existing Linux workspaces do not need conversion before they are opened on Windows. A seven-day preview preceded this release.

article.text: Correction: Pine's team plan supports 60 active projects, not the 100 projects stated in the October 7 launch post. The company says the earlier number counted archived projects and has updated the pricing table. Active projects beyond 60 require the enterprise plan. The correction does not change the storage allowance, user limit, or launch date. Customers who created more than 60 active projects during the first day will receive direct guidance. No other plan limits were revised. The corrected pricing page was observed on October 8, 2026.

cases.description: Two independently sourced parts of one protocol rollout plus an unrelated distractor.

article.text: Lumen published version 1.0 of the Lantern synchronization protocol on October 8, 2026. The specification defines the wire format, conflict markers, and a compatibility test suite. Lumen's announcement names Orbit as the first independent client to pass that public suite. The protocol repository includes fixtures under a permissive license and records the exact suite revision used for the result. Passing the suite does not establish performance, security, or broad adoption. Lumen says two draft sections remain informational and are not required for compatibility.

Orbit released an independent Lantern 1.0 client and links to its passing result for Lumen's public compatibility suite. The client can exchange the suite's fixture documents with Lumen's reference implementation. Orbit labels the build a developer preview and advises against production data. Its post does not claim that Lumen sponsored the client or that either project acquired the other. Performance and security review remain outside the compatibility suite. Source code and reproducible build instructions are available for the preview.

Ceramic Keys announced a compact mechanical keyboard with a glazed case and replaceable switches. Preorders open later in October and shipping is estimated for December. The vendor lists three switch options and two case colors. No review samples or independent measurements are available. The case uses a two-piece ceramic shell with a brass mounting plate, while the firmware supports remapping over a wired connection. Replacement switches use a standard hot-swap socket. Regional prices and final shipping quantities remain unannounced.

supported_conclusions: Lumen published Lantern 1.0 and Orbit released an independent client that passed its public suite.
forbidden_inferences: The keyboard is part of Lantern.

reason.text: The Lantern 1.0 specification and its first independently tested client are one development.

cases.description: A rewrite of confirmed coverage plus stale, insufficient speculation.

article.text: A community guide walks through the Atlas offline conversion command and installation of the signed Linux packages. It adds screenshots of each terminal step and recommends validating a converted copy before removing Atlas 1.x. The author is a community member and does not cite a new maintainer release, availability change, evaluation, or correction. The guide uses the package checksums and commands from the October 7 maintainer documentation. It presents no measured result, new compatibility claim, or later product event.

An undated forum summary speculates that Atlas might add mobile packages someday, but it cites no maintainer statement, repository change, release artifact, or schedule. The post repeats a user's guess that mobile support would be convenient and discusses possible touch-screen layouts. No build, preview, test result, issue milestone, or availability change is linked. Replies ask whether the maintainers have commented, but none supplies a source. The page snapshot contains no date beyond the forum thread metadata recorded by the collector.
